# Appeal of Denial — Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-22**
**Member: Riley Foster | Member ID: W204716433**
**Reference number: POC-D5606CAED3-36942**
**Payer/Plan: Banner Health (Commercial/ACA), Arizona**
**Governing policy: eviCore CMM-315 Shoulder Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures** ([link](https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-02/EviCore_CMM-315%20Shoulder%20Surg%20Arthro_Final_V1.0.2025_Pub02.25.2025.pdf))

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of my prior authorization request for a rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), as stated in the notice dated 2026-08-22. My request for reconsideration is based on my medical records, which I believe show that this surgery is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to review this decision again.

## A note on the criteria used for this denial

The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I have reviewed the policy criteria that were made available to me for this appeal, and I want to be transparent: the specific medical-necessity criteria for rotator cuff repair itself were not among the excerpts provided to me. The excerpts I have relate to labral repair, biceps tenodesis, and arthroscopic/open procedures for shoulder instability and laxity — these are different procedures and diagnoses than the one my surgeon has recommended. Because of that, I am not able to quote the plan's specific rotator cuff repair criteria back to it here, and I do not want to misapply criteria written for a different condition. Instead, I am laying out the clinical facts in my own words and asking the plan to compare them against whatever internal criteria for rotator cuff repair actually governed this denial.

## What my records show

- **Imaging directly contradicts the stated denial reason.** An MRI of my shoulder performed on 2026-07-06 showed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm, with grade 2 fatty atrophy. This is a clear, structural finding — not an ambiguous or borderline imaging result — and it corresponds to the site and severity of my ongoing symptoms.

- **My symptoms and exam findings are consistent with the imaging.** I have had progressive shoulder pain for 18 months that has not improved with rest. On examination, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side, and my range of motion is limited by pain. I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height, and I cannot sleep on the affected side. These functional limitations line up directly with a full-thickness rotator cuff tear of the size and severity shown on my MRI.

- **I have already completed extensive conservative treatment.** I completed 10 weeks (24 visits) of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, from 2026-04-17 to 2026-06-26, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief. My conservative care was not a brief or token effort — it was sustained, provider-directed, and ultimately unsuccessful.

- **There is no evidence of other conditions that would explain my symptoms instead.** My records do not document infection, untreated substance use, or any competing diagnosis. My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

- **My surgeon has documented that this procedure is medically necessary.** Dr. Okafor, my orthopedic surgeon, has reviewed my imaging, exam findings, and treatment history and has determined that rotator cuff repair is the appropriate next step given the size of the tear, my level of functional impairment, and the failure of extended conservative management.

## What I am asking

I am asking Banner Health to reconsider this denial in light of the MRI findings, exam findings, and documented failure of conservative treatment described above. If the plan applied specific rotator cuff repair criteria under CMM-315 that were not shared with me, I respectfully ask that those criteria be identified so that I and my surgeon can address them directly.

I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-02-18** (180 days from the date of the denial notice). I will send this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter, or, if that is not available to me, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed from me or from Dr. Okafor's office to complete this review.

Sincerely,

**[Riley Foster]**
Member ID: W204716433
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
